title: What number comes after nine thousand?
description: Joseph counts bundles of one thousand tickets at a village fair. One more bundle comes and the video shows which number that is.
teaching_notes: One idea: nine thousand and one more thousand make ten thousand. Watch for the child who squeezes ten into the thousands column.

source: Keep adding a thousand to 1,000. Which number do you reach a
video_script.why: The child can count in thousands up to nine thousand but has not yet named the number after it.
video_script.substitution: Count the bundles one at a time, add one more thousand, and see that ten thousands bundle into one ten thousand.
video_script.anchor: Joseph's bundles of one thousand tickets at his village fair in Kerala
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu squeezes ten into the thousands column. A place holds one digit from nought to nine, so ten thousands need a new place.
video_script.payoff_line: ten thousand is the same as ten thousands

final_answer.value: 10,000, which is ten thousand and is 10 thousands
final_answer.spoken: ten thousand, which is the same as ten thousands

never_show: the your-turn answer 1,000 and ten hundreds
maths_rules: each bundle holds 1,000 tickets; the bundles are counted 1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000, 5,000, 6,000, 7,000, 8,000, 9,000
10 bundles of 1,000 make 10 thousands = 10,000, called ten thousand
slip: ten written in the Thousands column; a column holds one digit, 0 to 9
your turn: count by hundreds from 900; 900 + 100 = 1,000, which is 10 hundreds; never shown
video_script.design: One idea: one more thousand after 9,000 is 10,000. Wrong idea: ten squeezed into the Thousands column. Joseph's bundles stay as the anchor; the count builds on the stage.

beats.on_screen: a photo of the village fair sits behind as a dimmed backdrop and fades at the end of the beat; a small title card From your book; a ticket counter at a village fair; nine bundles of tickets stand in a row, each labelled one thousand; a tenth bundle waits at the side

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.fair: the ticket counter and nine bundles appear
marks.ask: the tenth bundle slides in beside the row with an empty bracket

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='fair'/>Joseph sells tickets at a village fair, in bundles of one thousand.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>He has counted nine bundles, which is nine thousand tickets.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>One more bundle comes. Which number is that, and how many thousands is it?

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: the bundles move to the stage and are counted one at a time; a running label grows 1,000, 2,000 up to 9,000

marks.add: each bundle lights up as the label grows

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Each new bundle that Joseph adds to the row makes one thousand more tickets.
<bookmark mark='low'/>Count with Joseph. One thousand, two thousand, three thousand, four thousand, five thousand.
<bookmark mark='high'/>Six thousand, seven thousand, eight thousand, nine thousand.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows a Th column with 10 inside it; the column border flashes; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.chintu: Chintu's bubble appears with ten in the Thousands column
marks.one: the column border flashes around one digit
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>One more bundle makes ten. I will write ten in the thousands column.
<bookmark mark='one'/>The thousands column holds one digit only, from nought to nine.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>A number as big as ten will not fit inside one single column.

beats.on_screen: the board shows 9,000 + 1,000 = 10,000; the ten bundles tie together into one big bundle

marks.tie: the ten bundles tie into one big bundle
marks.name: the line 10,000 and the answer card appear

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Add one more bundle of one thousand to the nine thousand tickets he has.
<bookmark mark='tie'/>Ten bundles of one thousand tie up into one big bundle.
<bookmark mark='name'/>We write it as a one with four zeros after it. It is called ten thousand, and ten thousand is the same as ten thousands.

beats.on_screen: the answer card reads 10,000 = 10 thousands; the big bundle and ten small bundles sit side by side

marks.same: the big bundle and the ten small bundles sit side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>The big bundle holds exactly the same tickets as ten small bundles of one thousand each.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Ten thousand and ten thousands are two names for one and the same number.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the fair counter; two lines appear: each step adds one thousand; nine thousand and one more thousand make ten thousand; then a new count by hundreds with an empty box

marks.one: the line each step adds one thousand appears
marks.two: the line nine thousand and one more thousand make ten thousand appears

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Counting by thousands, each step adds one thousand.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Nine thousand and one more thousand make ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>Your turn. Count by hundreds. What number comes after nine hundred, and how many hundreds is it?
